desc.ma: Simple moving averages; stack several to read alignment
desc.ema: Weights recent prices more, turns faster

desc.st: ATR trailing stop that flips direction

desc.macd: Fast minus slow EMA with a histogram
desc.kdj: K, D and J stochastic lines

hint.ma: Averages stacked in order from short to long mark a bullish alignment; a pullback that holds the mid-term average is a common continuation entry.
hint.ema: EMA reacts to the latest prices sooner, suited to short timeframes; compare it with the same-period MA to read momentum.
hint.boll: A narrowing band often precedes a big move; riding the upper band is not overbought in a trend.
hint.donch: Buy the upper break, sell the lower one: one of the oldest trend rules (Turtles used 20 / 55). The bands exclude the current bar, matching the backtester.
hint.vwap: The institutional cost benchmark: price above VWAP means buyers are in control. Anchors reset each trading day (UTC+8).
hint.st: Line below price is bullish, above is bearish; many traders use it directly as a trailing stop.
hint.sar: Dots below price hold longs, above hold shorts; flips often in ranges, so filter with a trend indicator.
hint.rsi: In a trend RSI can sit above 70 for a long time; a bearish divergence matters more than a plain overbought reading.
hint.macd: Histogram turning positive is the golden cross; crosses above the zero line are more reliable.
hint.kdj: J is the most sensitive line; beyond 100 or below 0 usually marks a short-term extreme.
hint.cci: Beyond ±100 is the strong zone; falling back inside from +100 is a common exit.
hint.wr: Mirror image of the KDJ K value; -20 / -80 are the usual thresholds.
hint.atr: Stops 1.5 to 2 ATR away clear normal noise; it also underpins the ticket's risk-percent sizing.
hint.volume: Volume confirms price: breakouts on volume are credible, new highs on thin volume are suspect.
hint.obv: OBV making a new high before price signals money moving in early.
hint.xmab: A user-provided indicator formula: highs and lows each get a double XMA(N); their gap widens the bands (×P1/P2) and the overbought/oversold lines (+1.2 more). Bands turn green when both step down.

unreachable.title: Backend unreachable
unreachable.body: The admin console can't reach the backend, so users probably can't load the site either. The backend watchdog restarts it automatically within about 2 minutes: wait a few minutes, then refresh this page. If it hasn't recovered after 5 minutes, contact Rex.

hint.ok: If this page loads, the backend is alive. If it hangs, the watchdog restarts it within about 2 minutes.

hint.warn: The database is slow, so pages feel sluggish. Usually peak load; contact Rex if it lasts over 30 minutes.
hint.down: The database is unreachable and the whole site will error. Restarting the backend won't help; don't keep restarting it. Contact Rex.

hint.warn: Responding slowly; just keep an eye on it.
hint.down: Redis isn't responding, which causes odd symptoms like "close all" finding no positions or sentiment showing "-". The watchdog notifies Rex; contact Rex.

hint.warn: Working, with a minor issue: one failed check, or not all query channels connected (queries slow down at peak). This also shows for a few seconds right after "Reconnect MT5". Tell Rex if it lasts over 10 minutes.
hint.down: Direct-connect accounts can't trade right now. The VPS watchdog acts within about 90 seconds, and the gateway reconnects to the broker on its own, restarting itself within 15 minutes at most. Still red after 10 minutes usually means a broker-side problem: don't keep restarting, contact Rex.
hint.idle: The backend just started and hasn't checked the gateway yet. Wait a few seconds.

hint.warn: The feed is lagging; check whether charts are still moving.
hint.down: The feed has stopped and everyone's charts are frozen. On the market-feed PC check: (1) the MT5 terminal is open and logged in; (2) the feed EA is still attached to its chart (smiley in the chart's top-right corner); (3) the "Algo Trading" toolbar button is on. This light turns green within a minute once fixed. If unsure, contact Rex.
hint.idle: The backend hasn't received a quote yet. Normal right after a restart; wait a minute.

hint.ok: Signals are market-driven, so a quiet spell isn't necessarily a fault. If there are none for more than half a trading day, check that the 5 signal-EA charts on the market-feed PC are still open.
hint.warn: Can't read signal records, most likely a database problem; see the database light.

hint.ok: Settlement, competition rankings, email broadcasts and other background jobs are running normally.
hint.warn: A job reported an error recently (yellow below). Once in a while is fine; if it keeps erroring, send Rex a screenshot.
hint.down: A background job has stopped (red below), so its feature no longer updates automatically. Send Rex a screenshot; don't restart anything yourself yet.
hint.idle: The backend just started; jobs haven't run yet.

runbook.title: What to do when something breaks
runbook.intro: Check the lights above first, then find the matching case below. Don't act on anything marked "Contact Rex".

siteDown.q: The whole site won't load, or says "cannot connect to server"
siteDown.a: The backend watchdog restarts the backend within about 2 minutes. Try again after 5 minutes; if it still fails, contact Rex.

after502.q: Pages show 502 and recover a few seconds later
after502.a: Normal while the backend restarts. Only a 502 lasting over a minute is a problem.

chartsFrozen.a: Check the "Market feed" light above. If it's red, follow the steps next to it on the market-feed PC.

noSignals.q: No new signals for a long time
noSignals.a: Signals are market-driven and naturally sparse in quiet markets. If none for more than half a trading day, check that the 5 signal-EA charts are still open.

gatewayDown.q: Direct-connect accounts all show "not connected", or orders fail
gatewayDown.a: Check the "Gateway" light above. The watchdog handles it automatically; contact Rex if it's still red after 10 minutes.

reconnecting.q: Orders say "trading link reconnecting, please retry"
reconnecting.a: The gateway is reconnecting to the broker and that order was never sent. Retry in a few seconds.

unknownOutcome.q: After a restart some orders show "outcome unknown"
unknownOutcome.a: Tell the user to check their positions in MT5 first to see whether the order actually opened, before placing it again, to avoid a duplicate position.

appFrozen.q: The app shows no signals or frozen quotes, but the website is fine
appFrozen.a: Have the user fully close the app and reopen it, twice if needed.

bridgeOffline.q: A user's Bridge is offline, or says "no running MT5 terminal detected"
bridgeOffline.a: Have the user open MT5 and log in first, then restart the Bridge, and accept any update prompt.

bridge500.a: This is a server problem, not a bad token. Don't have the user reset the token. Send Rex a screenshot.

emailStuck.q: An email broadcast is stuck on "sending"
emailStuck.a: When the daily quota runs out it resumes automatically at 08:00 Beijing time; the Email tab also has a "Resume" button. Otherwise contact Rex.

mainland.q: All mainland China users can't connect, overseas users are fine
mainland.a: The Hong Kong edge node is down or expired. Admins can't fix this; contact Rex.

readOnly.q: The whole site is read-only, or shows 402
readOnly.a: A database quota or billing problem. Contact Rex.

backendBroken.q: The backend won't start, keeps restarting, or shows a database / migration error
backendBroken.a: Do not restart it again: another restart here can lose data. Contact Rex immediately.

strategy.title: Custom Strategies
strategy.subtitle: Pick a template, tune it, backtest against real historical prices, then enable it — once enabled, you'll get a signal only you can see whenever the condition is met.
strategy.proOnlyHint: Custom strategies are a PRO-exclusive feature
strategy.name: Strategy Name (optional)
strategy.maxReached: You've reached the limit of {{n}} strategies per user
strategy.condLimit: At the {{max}}-condition limit; remove one to add another.
strategy.condBothDirections: Applies to both directions (volatility has no direction)
strategy.condShortHint: Short-side conditions are mirrored automatically; no separate setup needed.
strategy.singlePairHint: One strategy watches one symbol on one timeframe. Cover more by creating more, each with its own performance stats.
strategy.legacyRulesReset: This strategy was built with the old rule format, which can't be converted to the new condition structure, so its original conditions weren't kept. Below is a starting condition — reconfigure it before saving and enabling.

strategy.flowTitle: Build a strategy in three steps
strategy.flowStep1Desc: Choose a symbol and timeframe, then pick the entry conditions. Not sure what to pick? Start from a recommended strategy.
strategy.flowStep2Desc: Run it over real history and read the win rate, trading costs and out-of-sample section before enabling anything.
strategy.flowStep3Desc: Once enabled, every match sends a signal only you can see — with one-click ordering.
strategy.stepBasicsHint: Decide which symbol and timeframe this strategy watches.
strategy.stepConditionsHint: A signal fires only when these are met. Start with one or two — more conditions mean fewer triggers.
strategy.stepRiskHint: Every signal carries a stop-loss and take-profit price; this sets how far they sit from the entry.
strategy.stepReviewHint: Run it over history and check the result is acceptable before you save and enable.
strategy.stepNeedConditions: Keep at least one entry condition to continue.
strategy.advancedHint: These all work left at their defaults — skipping them is fine.
strategy.presetPickHint: Six common playbooks. Once loaded, every condition and parameter stays editable. If in doubt, take MA trend — it's the easiest to read.
strategy.presetBlankHint: Already know which indicators you want? Go straight to the editor.
strategy.stopLossHint: Cut the trade once it moves this far against you — it caps the loss per signal.
strategy.takeProfitHint: Close the trade once it moves this far in your favour. R is a multiple of the stop distance, so 2R means twice the stop.
strategy.oneTradeHint: Recommended on: only one trade is followed at a time, so signals don't pile up.
strategy.coverageLoading: Checking how much history is actually available…
strategy.coverageFeedInactive: No live feed for this symbol right now, so its history won't grow — the backtest only reflects what's already stored.
strategy.btInsufficient: Not enough candle history to backtest: only {{bars}} candles exist for the {{requested}} days requested. History accrues while the feed is online — try again later.
strategy.btTotalCost: Trading costs deducted in this run: ${{cost}} (spread + slippage + commission)
strategy.btCostHint: Costs use the spread, slippage and per-lot commission configured for this symbol: entries take half the spread plus one slippage in the trade's direction, stop-outs take one more slippage penalty, and commission is charged once per round trip.
strategy.btSampleHint: History is always split in chronological order into the first 70% and the last 30%, each with its own metrics. Materially worse out-of-sample results mean the parameters were fitted, not discovered.
strategy.overfitWinRateDrop: Overfit risk: the out-of-sample win rate is more than 15 points below the in-sample one. These parameters likely just fit the first 70% of the history.
strategy.overfitReturnFlip: Overfit risk: profitable in-sample, loss-making out-of-sample. These parameters likely just fit the first 70% of the history.
strategy.overfitNotEvaluated: Sample too small, overfit not evaluated — with fewer than 10 resolved trades on either side, a win-rate difference is noise.
strategy.overfitClear: Out-of-sample performance is close to in-sample; no overfit flag.
strategy.symbolNotFed: No live feed for this symbol, so it can't be evaluated
strategy.optionalZeroHint: Enter 0 to disable any of the three. Timeout exit settles at the close once a position has run the set number of bars without touching SL/TP, so one stuck trade doesn't hold the "one trade at a time" slot indefinitely.
strategy.sessionWrapHint: Spans midnight: starts same day, ends the next. Entries are only allowed within this window, keyed off the bar's open time (UTC+8)
strategy.sessionHint: Entries are only allowed within this window, keyed off the bar's open time (UTC+8)
strategy.sessionTzNote: Times are UTC+8, matching the rest of the app
strategy.presetStartHint: Start from a preset and tweak it, or build from blank. A preset is just a set of starting values — the rules stay fully editable.
strategy.templateMaTrendDesc: Buy when price crosses above EMA20, sell on a cross below — the most basic form of trend following.
strategy.templateMacdCrossDesc: Buy when MACD crosses above its signal line, sell on a cross below — the classic momentum-confirmation signal.
strategy.templateRsiReversalDesc: Buy when RSI crosses back above the oversold level, sell when it crosses below the overbought level — betting on reversals.
strategy.templateBollingerBreakoutDesc: Buy when the close breaks above the upper band, sell when it breaks below the lower band — betting on breakout continuation.
strategy.templateDonchianBreakoutDesc: Buy when price makes a new high over the last N bars, sell on a new low — the core rule of the classic turtle-trading system.
strategy.templateMacdRsiComboDesc: MACD above zero sets the direction while RSI stays out of overbought, so you don't chase an overheated move.
strategy.oneTradeAtATimeOnHint: No new signal fires while the previous one hasn't hit its SL/TP yet.
strategy.oneTradeAtATimeOffHint: A new signal fires whenever the entry condition is met, regardless of whether the previous one has closed.
strategy.openPositionNotice: The strategy has {{count}} signal(s) still "open" — none of them have hit their stop-loss or take-profit yet, so they aren't counted in the stats below. That doesn't mean the strategy stopped firing; these just haven't resolved yet (with "one trade at a time" off, several can be independently open at once — each one is listed below). Re-run the backtest once more history has built up and you'll typically see completed trades.
strategy.overlayHint: Only the indicators this strategy's conditions use, with the same parameters you set on them. Switch one on to see what it read at each marker.
strategy.chartHint: {{n}} trades, marked on the chart below (green arrow = buy entry, red arrow = sell entry, dot = exit; amber arrow = fired but hasn't hit SL/TP yet, not counted in the stats)
strategy.chartHintCapped: {{n}} trades total. To keep the chart responsive, only the most recent {{shown}} are marked below; the stats above and the trade table below still cover all {{n}}.
strategy.deleteConfirm: Delete this strategy? Past signals it already fired are unaffected.
strategy.noSignals: No signals fired yet — once a strategy is enabled, matching signals will appear here automatically
strategy.clearSignalsConfirm: Clear the entire fired-signal history? This doesn't affect the strategies' enabled state — the dashboard and signals page will be cleared too.
strategy.flowLead: Pick conditions, verify against real prices, then enable.
strategy.disclaimer: Strategy signals fire only when your conditions are met — a read-only judgement that never places an order by itself. Backtests do account for spread, slippage and commission as configured, but not for overnight swap, and they do not simulate rejections or execution latency. Nothing here is a promise of returns, and past performance does not predict future results.

cashflowRules.title: How deposits and withdrawals count
cashflowRules.hint: Withdrawing never erases what you earned; depositing can't inflate your rank
cashflowRules.lead: Return = profit ÷ how much was in the account at the time. Every trade is scored on its own, against the capital in the account while that trade was open — not the balance at the start or end of the period.
cashflowRules.formula: A trade's capital = the larger of what was in the account when it opened and when it closed

case1.w: The account held 10,000 while trading; the withdrawal came later and doesn't touch a finished result.

case2.w: The money you took out never backed this trade, so it isn't used as a denominator to hold you down.

case3.t: Withdraw while a position is open
case3.w: Scored on the 10,000 it opened with — the larger moment wins, so moving money mid-trade changes nothing.

case4.t: Deposit while a position is open
case4.s: 1,000 at open → top up to 10,000 → close for 500
case4.w: Scored on the 10,000 it closed with — the larger moment again, so a deposit can't make the return look better.

cashflowRules.noteSmall: Small drops aren't withdrawals: commission, swap and similar odds and ends are ignored. A drop counts as a withdrawal only when it exceeds both 100 USD and 5% of the account's capital.
cashflowRules.noteFloor: An account below {{usd}} USD of capital doesn't rank — this keeps figures like "earned 500 on 300, up 167%" off the board.
cashflowRules.noteWinRate: The win-rate board is unaffected by cash flows: it only counts how many trades you won and lost.
cashflowRules.noteSealedBoard: Once a period ends its results are sealed; no later deposit, withdrawal or trade can change a finished ranking.
cashflowRules.noteSealedComp: Once a competition ends, the settled result is final; later deposits, withdrawals and trades no longer move it.
cashflowRules.noteNoFlow: For accounts that never deposit or withdraw, the calculation is exactly what it always was.
